extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer-algebra system (beginners to intermediate mathematicians/computational algebraists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules for entering and running Magma commands interactively, creating algebraic structures (magmas) and elements, interpreting example sessions, and quitting the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement termination: semicolon required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each complete statement must finish with a semicolon (;).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma will not execute (perform) the statement(s) on the current line until the return key has been pressed. If there is no output, the most likely reason is that the semicolon at the end of the line has been forgotten. In this case, the user should type a semicolon, and then press the return key. Example: '2 + 4;' produces output '6'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of statements and use of return key
rubrics_metrics.description: It is customary to place each statement on a separate line, by pressing the return key after the semicolon, except in the case of a succession of short statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although statements may be put together in other ways, Magma will not execute the current line until the return key is pressed, so pressing return after each (complete) statement is the normal interactive practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt semantics and example formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever Magma is ready to receive a statement it displays a prompt symbol (usually '>') on the left of the input line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any line beginning with a prompt symbol has been typed by the user (not including the prompt itself), and any line without the prompt symbol at the beginning is Magma’s response to the user’s input. Examples in the book follow this convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering the Magma system
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the user can enter Magma by going to a shell prompt and typing the word 'magma' then pressing return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this does not work, local experts should be consulted for advice on how Magma is installed at the user's institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quitting Magma
rubrics_metrics.description: The command for finishing a Magma session is 'quit;'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semicolon, followed by the return key, is compulsory. An alternative method of quitting is to type the control-d character at the beginning of a line; in that case pressing return is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating magmas before creating elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Since all computation in Magma takes place in one or more algebraic structures, the first step in any computation involves defining the necessary magmas (algebraic structures). Once the magmas have been defined, elements and other related objects of these magmas may be created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are certain automatically-created magmas, such as the ring of integers and the monoid of character strings, which need not be defined explicitly prior to working with their elements. Examples: 'Z := IntegerRing();', 'P<x> := PolynomialRing(Z);', 'S6 := SymmetricGroup(6);'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing objects by typing their identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: After assignments, objects may be printed by typing their identifier at the prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after 'P<x> := PolynomialRing(Z);' typing 'P;' prints 'Univariate Polynomial Algebra in x over Integer Ring'. This is the standard way to request Magma to display a representation of an object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosing missing/incorrect output
rubrics_metrics.description: If output different to the example appears on the user's screen, then a typing error has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no output, check for a missing semicolon. If output is present but different, correct the typing error and try again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation convention for worked examples in the manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of Magma interactive sessions presented in this book are displayed with the prompt/input/output convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should interpret lines beginning with '>' as user input (excluding the prompt itself) and lines without it as Magma output. This convention is used consistently throughout the examples in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult online help and environment chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: There are several short-cuts and other ways of making the user’s task easier when using Magma; these are described in Chapter 11 (online help) and Chapter 15 (user environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These techniques are not strictly essential for operating Magma, but the reader is advised to glance at these chapters soon and study them in detail later to improve efficiency.
